summary: Extends the OAuth 2.0 framework with request parameters that let a client tell the authorization server which protected resource or resources it wants access to. The server can then issue tokens suited to those resources.

eli5.summary: When asking for a pass, you say which building you want to enter, so the pass you get is made for that one place.

questions: what is the oauth resource parameter
how to audience restrict an oauth access token
subtitle: A resource parameter that lets an OAuth client say which API a requested token is meant for.

tldr.problem: An OAuth authorization server often does not know where a client will use the access token it requests, so it cannot tailor, encrypt or audience-restrict the token for that resource.
tldr.mechanism: The client adds one or more resource parameters, each an absolute URI naming the target resource, to authorization and token requests. The server can then restrict the token to that audience, and uses invalid_target for bad values.
tldr.outcome: Tokens can be made valid only at the intended resources, reducing the chance that one resource reuses a token elsewhere.

today: RFC 8707 is a Proposed Standard (Standards Track, February 2020). The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Name the Resource
sections.content:
Experience with the OAuth 2.0 framework showed that, for example when an authorization server serves many diverse resources, the client should tell it where it intends to use the access token. Knowing the protected resource lets the server build the token for it, such as encrypting the token to that resource, and honour different data requirements per resource.

It also improves security. A bearer token lets anyone holding it get access, so it should be valid only at a specific resource and scope. If the server knows the resource, it can restrict the token's audience so it fails elsewhere.

OAuth scope is sometimes stretched to name a location, but scope is typically about what access is wanted, such as email or channels:read, not where it will be used. Some deployments already use proprietary parameters for this. This RFC offers a standard, interoperable one.
sections.eli5: A token is like a key. A key that says which door it opens is safer than one that opens any door.

sections.title: The resource Parameter
sections.content:
A client MAY include resource in requests to the authorization server. Its value MUST be an absolute URI and MUST NOT include a fragment. It SHOULD NOT include a query component, though the RFC allows it where useful. Multiple resource parameters MAY be used for a token meant for several resources.

The client SHOULD give the most specific URI it can for the whole API it wants, normally the API's base URI. The RFC's examples: https://api.example.com/ for an exclusive host, https://api.example.com/app/ if the host has many applications, and https://apps.example.com/scim/ to cover all the SCIM endpoints.

The error code invalid_target means the requested resource is invalid, missing, unknown or malformed. The server SHOULD audience-restrict issued tokens to the indicated resources, for instance using the aud claim in a JWT. It may use the exact value as the audience or map it to a more general identifier.
sections.eli5: You write the address of the place you want to visit on your request form. If the address is wrong or unknown, you get an 'invalid target' answer.

sections.title: Authorization and Token Requests
sections.content:
In an authorization request, resource says which resources access is wanted for. With the implicit flow it applies to the returned access token; with the code flow it applies to the full authorization grant. If it is omitted, the server MAY use no specific resource or a default, or MAY require it and fail with invalid_target. It might also use the value to tell the user which resources the client will access.

In a token request, for all grant types, resource says where the token will be used. Which values are acceptable is at the server's sole discretion. For refresh_token or authorization_code grants, policy may limit them to the resources originally granted or a subset. For a subset, the access token covers the subset, while any refresh token stays bound to the full original grant.

If both resource and scope are sent, the token should be usable with that scope at all the requested resources, effectively the cartesian product. The server should downscope the token to what each resource needs and must report the effective scope in the response if it differs from the request.
sections.eli5: You can ask for a pass for the library first, then later ask for a different pass for the gym. Each pass is cut down to what that place needs.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC shows a code-flow authorization request with scope=calendar contacts and two resource parameters, https://cal.example.com/ and https://contacts.example.com/. The client then redeems the code at the token endpoint with resource=https://cal.example.com/ and receives a token with scope of calendar.

Later it uses the refresh token with resource=https://contacts.example.com/. The new token has scope of contacts and an expiry of 3600 seconds. In both responses the JWT access token carries the matching audience.
sections.eli5: One request asks for both calendar and contacts. Later the client trades in for one pass that works only at the calendar and another that works only at the contacts.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
An audience-restricted token that is legitimately presented to a resource cannot then be taken by that resource and used elsewhere. For multi-tenant or user-content servers, the resource URI should include whatever identifies the tenant, such as a path component, so tokens cannot cross tenants.

Using a single resource value is encouraged. A bearer token with several audiences works at all of them, so any one can use it against the others, which requires a high degree of trust. The value should correspond to the resource's network-addressable location where feasible, so the client can check who controls it. With an abstract identifier, the client must validate out of band that endpoints receiving tokens are the intended audience.

On privacy, the authorization server already sees a lot of user and client behaviour. Without token introspection, the resource parameter may allow somewhat more granular tracking.
sections.eli5: A pass for one shop is safer than a pass for many shops, because any shop that holds a many-shop pass could use it at the others.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA is asked to update the OAuth Parameters registry with the parameter name resource, used in authorization requests and token requests. The OAuth Extensions Error registry gets the error invalid_target, used in implicit grant error responses and token error responses. The change controller for both is the IESG, and the specification document is RFC 8707.
sections.eli5: The new form field and the new error message get written into the official lists, so everyone uses the same names.
